chunk_findings.detail: `own_lapsed` is defined as `existing is not None and existing.holder == holder and cfg.lease.resume_own` — it never checks that the lease actually lapsed. The knob's doc says "The agent whose lease LAPSED resumes it", and the very branch being bypassed distinguishes the two cases (`if existing.expired_at:` with an implied else for a live lease). So a plain `ddflow claim` of an item whose lease is still live and held by the same agent now skips the `reclaim_policy == "report"` handling entirely and falls through to the code path intended for fresh/resumed claims, instead of the existing-lease path. Given a live lease on T1 held by "first" and `resume_own` left at its default `true`, `LC.claim(repo, "T1", agent="first")` bypasses the branch that previously handled "you already hold this", changing behavior for a case the feature never targeted. The condition should also require the lease to be expired (e.g. `existing.expired_at is not None` or equivalent) before short-circuiting.
